name: Wikidata
summary: Wikimedia's open knowledge base of structured facts: look up items and properties by label, read an item's labels, statements and sitelinks, and run SPARQL queries over the whole graph.

user_agent.description: A descriptive User-Agent with contact details, e.g. 'MyAgent/1.0 (you@example.com)'; Wikimedia blocks clients without one, so set your own for regular use.

notes: Keyless for reads. Wikimedia's User-Agent policy applies to both hosts: a generic or missing User-Agent can be blocked; set WIKIDATA_USER_AGENT with your contact details.
Ids: items are Q-numbers (Q42), properties P-numbers (P31 instance of, P569 date of birth). Find ids with the search calls, then read the item.
The REST API is versioned in the path (wikibase/v1); its rate limits follow MediaWiki's and are not published as numbers.

SPARQL: 60 seconds of query time per 60 seconds per client (User-Agent plus IP), 5 parallel queries per IP, 30 failing queries per minute, and each query is cut off at 60 seconds. 429 carries Retry-After; ignoring it can get a temporary ban.

endpoints.name: Search items by label
endpoints.summary: Items whose label or alias matches a term in one language, with their ids and descriptions.

q.description: Term to match against labels and aliases.

endpoints.name: Suggest items by label prefix
endpoints.summary: Items whose label or alias starts with the typed prefix, for autocomplete.

endpoints.name: Search properties by label
endpoints.summary: Properties (P-ids) whose label or alias matches a term, to find the property a statement or SPARQL query needs.

q.description: Term to match against labels and aliases.

endpoints.name: Get an item
endpoints.summary: One item's labels, descriptions and aliases in every language, its statements and its sitelinks.

_fields.description: Comma-separated parts to return: type, labels, descriptions, aliases, statements, sitelinks.

notes: A whole item is large (every language); pass _fields or use the labels and statements calls to keep it small.

endpoints.name: Get an item's statements
endpoints.summary: The item's statements (property, value, qualifiers, references), optionally for one property only.

property.description: One property id to keep, e.g. P569.

notes: Values that are items come back as ids only; read their labels with items.label.

endpoints.name: Get an item's label in one language, with fallback
endpoints.summary: The item's label in a language, falling back to a related language when it has none.

endpoints.name: Get an item's sitelinks
endpoints.summary: The Wikipedia and other Wikimedia pages about the item, by site id (enwiki, dewiki...).

endpoints.name: Get a property
endpoints.summary: One property's data type, labels, descriptions, aliases and statements.

_fields.description: Comma-separated parts to return: type, data_type, labels, descriptions, aliases, statements.

endpoints.name: Run a SPARQL query
endpoints.summary: Results of a SPARQL query over the whole Wikidata graph (lists, joins, counts across items).

query.example: SELECT ?item ?itemLabel WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q146. SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". } } LIMIT 5

format.description: json for SPARQL JSON results; the default is XML.

notes: Pass format=json, or results come back as XML.
GET answers are cached; use sparql.query_post only for queries too long for a URL.

endpoints.name: Run a long SPARQL query over POST
endpoints.summary: The same query service as sparql.query, for queries too long for a URL.

query.description: The SPARQL query, sent as the form field query.

format.description: json for SPARQL JSON results; the default is XML.

notes: A read: POST only carries a long query past URL limits, and the query service is read-only (SPARQL SELECT/ASK/CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE; it changes nothing).
POST answers are not cached, so prefer GET when the query fits in a URL.
